headline: The Trains, Buses & Transit Master 20
threshold: By Lesson 20, you can teach a companion how a transit system works, fix a wrong-station or missing-seat problem with staff, lead a tired group through a disruption, report an incident or near miss calmly, and write a formal complaint in Spanish.

lessons.title: Explain the CDMX Metro and Metrobús to a Newcomer
lessons.objective: Explain step by step, with reasons, how the Metro and Metrobús connect for a friend new to Mexico City.

words.note: In CDMX the same card works on the Metro and the Metrobús.
CDMX Metro word for a station where two lines connect.
Metro directions take the name of the last station: dirección Indios Verdes.
Every CDMX Metro station has its own picture symbol.
Mexico and the US say hora pico; Spain says hora punta.

words.en: the stretch, the leg of the trip

words.note: Use it to contrast the two systems: el Metro va bajo tierra; en cambio, el Metrobús...

words.en: First we go down to the Metro, and then we come out to the Metrobús.
words.es: Primero bajamos al Metro y luego salimos al Metrobús.

words.en: The Metrobús runs in its own lane; that's why it's fast.
words.es: El Metrobús va por su propio carril, por eso es rápido.

words.en: We use the same card because it works on both systems.
words.es: Usamos la misma tarjeta porque sirve en los dos sistemas.

words.en: Look at the name of the end station; that's how you know the direction.
words.es: Fíjate en el nombre de la terminal; así sabes la dirección.
words.note: Informal (tú), for a friend.

words.en: At the transfer station, follow the color of the new line.
words.es: En la correspondencia, sigue el color de la línea nueva.

words.en: Almost: the Metrobús doesn't run underground, it runs on the street.
words.es: Casi: el Metrobús no va bajo tierra, va por la calle.

words.en: Can you explain the route back to me, from start to finish?
words.es: ¿Me explicas la ruta otra vez, de principio a fin?

words.en: At rush hour it's packed, so we're leaving with time to spare.
words.es: En hora pico va lleno, por eso salimos con tiempo.

lessons.speaking: You are showing Lucía around, and the AI is Lucía, a friend on her first day in Mexico City: explain the route to Coyoacán step by step with primero, luego, porque and por eso, then have her explain it back and correct her gently.

grammar.focus: Connectors for sequence and cause (primero, luego, porque, por eso)

examples.es: Primero tomamos el Metro y luego caminamos a la estación del Metrobús.
examples.en: First we take the Metro, and then we walk to the Metrobús station.

examples.es: En el Metrobús no se paga en efectivo; por eso cargamos la tarjeta.
examples.en: You can't pay cash on the Metrobús; that's why we put money on the card.

lessons.title: Read TransMilenio Route Codes Before Boarding
lessons.objective: Read a TransMilenio route board and explain which services stop where and why some skip stations.

words.note: In TransMilenio, a vagón is a section of the station where certain services stop.
TransMilenio service that stops at every station on its corridor.
Bus that links neighborhoods to a portal.
Bogotá signs say sentido norte-sur or sur-norte.

words.en: This is where you catch the buses heading south.
words.es: Aquí se toman los buses hacia el sur.

words.en: If the code doesn't show our station, that bus is no good for us.
words.es: Si el código no muestra nuestra estación, ese bus no nos sirve.

words.en: That express doesn't stop at our station, Joaquín.
words.es: Ese expreso no para en nuestra estación, Joaquín.

words.en: Let's take the all-stops service instead; it stops at every station.
words.es: Mejor tomemos la ruta fácil, que para en todas.

words.en: Which platform section do you catch this service from?
words.es: ¿En qué vagón se toma este servicio?

words.en: The expresses skip stations so they can go faster.
words.es: Los expresos no paran en todas para ir más rápido.

words.en: Excuse me, does this service run at this time?
words.es: Disculpe, ¿este servicio funciona a esta hora?
words.note: Formal (usted), for station staff.

lessons.speaking: You are reading the route board at Portal Norte, and the AI is Joaquín, a fellow volunteer: explain which services stop where and why some skip stations, using structures like aquí se toma and si es expreso, no para, then agree on the right service.

grammar.focus: Impersonal se; si + present for general truths (aquí se sube, si es expreso no para)

examples.es: Aquí se entra con la tarjeta y se busca el vagón del servicio.
examples.en: Here you go in with your card and look for the service's platform section.

examples.es: Si es expreso, no para en todas las estaciones.
examples.en: If it's an express, it doesn't stop at every station.

lessons.title: Teach a Friend to Top Up and Tap a SUBE Card
lessons.objective: Coach a friend through topping up and tapping a transit card, then check their teach-back for errors.

words.note: In Argentina you cargar la SUBE, meaning you put money on it.
For a woman: la kiosquera.
Argentine word for a city bus.
The device on the bus or at the turnstile where you tap the card.
An online top-up you must tap at a terminal or reader before you can use it.

words.en: Give it to the kiosk owner and tell him how much you want to put on it.
words.es: Dásela al kiosquero y dile cuánto quieres cargar.

words.en: Hold it flat on the reader and wait for the beep.
words.es: Apóyala bien y espera el pitido.
words.note: Porteños say apoyala, cargala (vos form); the tú form is understood everywhere.

words.en: Keep the receipt, just in case.
words.es: El comprobante, guárdalo por si acaso.

words.en: Now you explain it to me, step by step.
words.es: Ahora explícamelo tú, paso por paso.

words.en: On the bus, tell the driver where you're going before you tap it.
words.es: En el colectivo, dile al chofer adónde vas antes de apoyarla.

words.en: If your balance isn't enough, no problem: we'll top it up.
words.es: Si no te alcanza el saldo, no pasa nada: la cargamos.

words.en: Excuse me, could you top up my SUBE, please?
words.es: Disculpe, ¿me carga la SUBE, por favor?
words.note: Formal (usted), for the kiosk owner.

lessons.speaking: You are teaching Camila, and the AI is Camila, a Uruguayan friend: walk her through topping up and tapping the SUBE with commands like cárgala, apóyala and no la saques todavía, then have her explain it back and correct any errors.

grammar.focus: Commands with object pronouns (cárgala, apóyala, no la saques todavía)

examples.es: Cárgala en el kiosco antes de subir al colectivo.
examples.en: Top it up at the kiosk before you get on the bus.

examples.es: No la saques todavía; déjala hasta que suene.
examples.en: Don't take it off yet; leave it there until it beeps.

lessons.title: Read the Bus Company's Rules Before an Overnight Ride
lessons.objective: Read a long-distance bus company's boarding conditions and explain what to do before and after check-in.

words.note: Used for both men and women: la titular for a woman.
Common loanword in Peru for a bus company's check-in desk.
Bus with seats that recline almost flat.
Peruvian usage for moving a ticket to another date.

words.en: We need to check the name before we get to the check-in desk.
words.es: Hay que revisar el nombre antes de llegar al counter.

words.en: After we check in, we hand over the suitcases for the hold.
words.es: Después de registrarnos, entregamos las maletas para la bodega.

words.en: Renata, your name on the ticket doesn't match your passport.
words.es: Renata, tu nombre en el pasaje no coincide con el pasaporte.

words.en: According to the conditions, we have to arrive before the check-in time.
words.es: Según las condiciones, hay que llegar antes de la hora de presentación.

words.en: Excuse me, what do you need to correct the name on the ticket?
words.es: Disculpe, ¿qué se necesita para corregir el nombre del pasaje?
words.note: Formal (usted), for the agent.

words.en: Is there a fee for the name change?
words.es: ¿Hay que pagar alguna penalidad por el cambio de nombre?
words.note: Formal (usted), for the agent.

words.en: Could you confirm that for me in writing, please?
words.es: ¿Me lo puede confirmar por escrito, por favor?
words.note: Formal (usted).

words.en: Before you get on the bus, keep the baggage tag somewhere safe.
words.es: Antes de subir al bus, guarda el ticket de equipaje.
words.note: Informal (tú), for your travel partner.

lessons.speaking: You are reading the boarding conditions with Renata, and the AI is Renata, your travel partner, and later Óscar, the agent: explain what to do before and after check-in with antes de, después de and hay que, and ask Óscar about any rule you're unsure of.

grammar.focus: Antes de / después de + infinitive; hay que (antes de embarcar hay que mostrar el documento)

examples.es: Antes de embarcar hay que mostrar el documento de identidad.
examples.en: Before boarding, you have to show your ID document.

examples.es: Después de pasar por el counter, hay que esperar en la sala de espera.
examples.en: After going through the check-in desk, you have to wait in the waiting room.

lessons.title: Ticket Says Chamartín, We Are at Atocha
lessons.objective: Explain at customer service how a wrong-station booking happened and propose a realistic fix.

words.note: Renfe's booking code, printed on the ticket and in the email.
In Spain a train ticket is el billete.
Madrid's commuter rail. It links Atocha and Chamartín.
In Spain, plaza is the usual word for a seat on a booking.
Informal but common: a moment of absent-mindedness.

words.en: I bought the ticket last night, very late, on my phone.
words.es: Compré el billete anoche, muy tarde, desde el móvil.

words.en: I thought the train left from Atocha.
words.es: Creía que el tren salía de Atocha.
words.note: Imperfect for what you believed; preterite for the action (compré).

words.en: I didn't notice the departure station.
words.es: No me fijé en la estación de origen.

words.en: Here is the booking reference and the confirmation email.
words.es: Aquí tiene el localizador y el correo de confirmación.
words.note: Formal: aquí tiene, to the agent.

words.en: Could you change it to a train that leaves from here?
words.es: ¿Podría cambiármelo a un tren que salga de aquí?
words.note: Formal conditional: polite way to ask for a fix.

words.en: If not, would I get to Chamartín on time by commuter train?
words.es: Si no, ¿llegaría a tiempo a Chamartín en Cercanías?

words.en: Would I have to pay the fare difference?
words.es: ¿Habría que pagar la diferencia de precio?

words.en: It was my slip-up, I'm sorry.
words.es: Fue un despiste mío, lo siento.

lessons.speaking: You are a traveler at Madrid Atocha customer service, and the AI is Begoña, the agent: explain how you booked the wrong station with the preterite and imperfect (lo compré anoche, creía que salía de aquí), then propose a realistic fix with ¿podría…?

grammar.focus: Preterite vs imperfect; conditional for the proposal (lo compré anoche, creía que salía de aquí, ¿podría cambiarlo?)

examples.es: Lo compré anoche y creía que salía de Atocha.
examples.en: I bought it last night and thought it left from Atocha.

examples.es: ¿Podría cambiármelo al siguiente tren desde aquí?
examples.en: Could you change it to the next train from here?

lessons.title: Our Reserved Coach Is Missing: Take a Substitute Seat
lessons.objective: Compare the substitute seats a conductor offers when your reserved coach isn't on the train, and choose.

words.note: On Chilean trains a coach is usually el coche.
For a woman: la acompañante.
Common in Chile and much of South America.

words.en: Is this seat going to be less comfortable than the reserved one?
words.es: ¿Este asiento va a ser más incómodo que el reservado?

words.en: If we take the next train, what time will we arrive in Chillán?
words.es: Si tomamos el próximo tren, ¿a qué hora llegaremos a Chillán?

words.en: Ignacio, we'll sit apart, but we'll still get there.
words.es: Ignacio, vamos a ir separados, pero llegaremos igual.
words.note: Informal, to your partner. Igual here means 'all the same'.

words.en: The next train is quieter, but we'll arrive later.
words.es: El próximo tren es más tranquilo, pero llegaremos más tarde.

words.en: Does this coach have more legroom than that one?
words.es: ¿Tiene más espacio para las piernas este coche que aquel?
words.note: Formal, to the conductor.

words.en: Is there any compensation for the seat change?
words.es: ¿Hay alguna compensación por el cambio de asiento?

words.en: Do I have to go to the ticket office to change the ticket?
words.es: ¿Tengo que pasar por la boletería para cambiar el pasaje?

words.en: We'll take the split seats, thanks.
words.es: Nos quedamos con los asientos separados, gracias.

lessons.speaking: You are a traveler on the platform at Santiago's Estación Central with your partner Ignacio, and the AI is Patricio, the conductor: compare the seats he offers using va a ser, más… que and llegaremos, check with Ignacio, then choose one.

grammar.focus: Future and ir a; comparisons (este va a ser más incómodo que aquel, llegaremos igual)

examples.es: Este asiento va a ser más incómodo que aquel.
examples.en: This seat is going to be less comfortable than that one.

examples.es: Si vamos por separado, llegaremos igual a Chillán.
examples.en: If we sit separately, we'll still get to Chillán.

lessons.title: Wallet Stolen on the Metro: Statement to Police
lessons.objective: Narrate a wallet theft to police in order, giving exact times, line, station, and card and phone numbers.

words.note: In Spain, the official report you file with police is la denuncia.
The noun stays the same for both genders; only the article changes with the officer's gender.
Spain's term; in Latin America it is la licencia de conducir.
This is the everyday word in Spain; Latin Americans usually say celular instead.

words.en: I got on the metro at Abando at 18:40.
words.es: Subí al metro en Abando a las 18:40.

words.en: I got off at the third stop and my wallet was gone.
words.es: Bajé en la tercera parada y ya no tenía la cartera.

words.en: A man shoved me when the doors closed.
words.es: Un hombre me dio un empujón cuando se cerraron las puertas.

words.en: The last 4 digits of the card are 3827.
words.es: Los últimos 4 dígitos de la tarjeta son 3827.
words.note: Say card digits one by one or in pairs, slowly.

words.es: Mi número de móvil es el +1 312 555 0147.
words.note: In Spain, phone numbers take el: es el 612...

words.en: Excuse me, it's my bank; I have to confirm the block.
words.es: Perdone, es mi banco; tengo que confirmar el bloqueo.
words.note: Formal: perdone, to the officer.

words.en: Could you repeat that more slowly, please?
words.es: ¿Me lo puede repetir más despacio, por favor?

words.en: Can you give me a copy of the report?
words.es: ¿Me puede dar una copia de la denuncia?

lessons.speaking: You are a traveler at an Ertzaintza station near Bilbao's Abando, and the AI is officer Ane Etxeberria: narrate the wallet theft in order with preterite verbs like subí and bajé, giving exact times, the line, the station, and your card and phone numbers.

grammar.focus: Preterite narration; numbers under pressure (subí a las 18:40, bajé en la tercera parada)

examples.es: Subí al metro a las 18:40 y bajé en la tercera parada.
examples.en: I got on the metro at 18:40 and got off at the third stop.

examples.es: Llamé al banco a las 19:05 y bloquearon la tarjeta.
examples.en: I called the bank at 19:05 and they blocked the card.

lessons.title: No, We Don't Cross the Tracks to Catch It
lessons.objective: Refuse a friend's unsafe shortcut across the tracks, give clear reasons, and lead them to the safe route.

words.note: Spain's term; in Latin America it is el tren de carga.
For a woman: la maquinista.
Common in Spain: lo han dicho por megafonía.
Tenemos tiempo de sobra = we have plenty of time.
Informal, to a man; to a woman: tranquila.

words.en: Diego, don't cross the tracks, seriously.
words.es: Diego, no cruces la vía, de verdad.
words.note: Informal tú command to a friend.

words.en: Don't get off the platform and move away from the edge; a train can pass without stopping.
words.es: No bajes del andén y aléjate del borde; puede pasar un tren sin parar.

words.en: I don't recommend you go down onto the tracks for anything.
words.es: No te recomiendo que bajes a la vía por nada.
words.note: No recomiendo que + subjunctive (bajes, cruces).

words.en: From the bend, the train driver wouldn't see us in time.
words.es: Desde la curva, el maquinista no nos vería a tiempo.

words.en: Excuse me, does the underpass go to platform 2?
words.es: Disculpe, ¿el paso subterráneo lleva al andén 2?
words.note: Formal, to the station worker.

words.en: Do we have time to get there through the underpass?
words.es: ¿Nos da tiempo a llegar por el paso subterráneo?
words.note: Common in Spain: ¿nos da tiempo a...?

words.en: Don't run on the stairs; let's go fast, but carefully.
words.es: No corras en las escaleras; vamos rápido, pero con cuidado.

words.en: Easy, if we miss it, we'll catch the next one.
words.es: Tranquilo, si lo perdemos, cogemos el siguiente.
words.note: In Spain coger is the normal verb for catching a train.

lessons.speaking: You are traveling with your friend Diego at a small station in Mérida, and the AI plays Diego and station worker Paqui: refuse the shortcut with negative commands like no cruces and no recomiendo que bajes, give clear reasons, and ask Paqui to confirm the underpass route.

grammar.focus: Negative commands; subjunctive after no recomiendo que (no cruces, no recomiendo que bajes a la vía)

examples.es: No cruces la vía; vamos por el paso subterráneo.
examples.en: Don't cross the tracks; let's take the underpass.

examples.es: No recomiendo que saltes del andén, Diego.
examples.en: I don't recommend you jump off the platform, Diego.

lessons.title: Feedback on a Friend's Too-Tight Itinerary
lessons.objective: Give a friend honest, kind feedback on their transit plan and recommend specific changes.

words.note: Common in Peru for short trips between towns.
Common in Latin America; same meaning as el retraso.
Common word in Peru for a hostel or guesthouse stay.
Used for schedules: un horario muy ajustado.

words.en: Valeria, I recommend you leave more of a time buffer.
words.es: Valeria, te recomiendo que dejes más margen de tiempo.
words.note: Informal: tú with a friend.

words.en: I love your plan, but the transfer is very tight.
words.es: Me encanta tu plan, pero el traslado está muy ajustado.

words.en: I suggest you take an earlier train.
words.es: Te sugiero que tomes un tren más temprano.

words.en: I'd rather we change it now, not at the station.
words.es: Prefiero que lo cambiemos ahora y no en la estación.

words.en: I hope the train arrives on time, but we can't count on it.
words.es: Ojalá que el tren llegue puntual, pero no podemos contar con eso.

words.en: It's not criticism; I just want you to arrive stress-free.
words.es: No es una crítica; solo quiero que llegues tranquila.

words.en: What if we book an extra night in Cusco?
words.es: ¿Y si reservamos una noche extra en Cusco?

words.en: It's your call; I'm just giving you my honest opinion.
words.es: Tú decides; yo solo te doy mi opinión sincera.

lessons.speaking: You are Valeria's travel friend, and the AI is Valeria: review her tight train-to-bus plan, say what works, and recommend specific changes with te recomiendo que…, te sugiero que… and prefiero que…, staying honest and kind.

grammar.focus: Present subjunctive after wishes and recommendations (te recomiendo que dejes margen, prefiero que lo cambiemos)

examples.es: Te recomiendo que dejes al menos 2 horas de margen.
examples.en: I recommend you leave at least 2 hours of buffer.

examples.es: Prefiero que lo cambiemos hoy mismo.
examples.en: I'd rather we change it today.

lessons.title: Two Friends, Two Departure Times: Settle It
lessons.objective: Report what each friend said, calm the argument, check the ticket, and get everyone on board together.

words.note: Standard word in Uruguay for city and long-distance buses.
Uruguay: common word for a staff member; a woman is la funcionaria.
Usual word for a numbered seat on Uruguayan buses.

words.en: Sofía said the bus left at 9.
words.es: Sofía dijo que el ómnibus salía a las 9.

words.en: Andrés thought it was later, at 9:30.
words.es: Andrés creía que era más tarde, a las 9:30.

words.en: Andrés said he had read a different time in the message.
words.es: Andrés dijo que había leído otra hora en el mensaje.

words.en: Neither of you is to blame; it was a misunderstanding.
words.es: Ninguno tiene la culpa; fue un malentendido.

words.en: Excuse me, what time does the bus to Punta del Este leave?
words.es: Disculpe, ¿a qué hora sale el ómnibus a Punta del Este?
words.note: Formal: usted with the clerk.

words.en: Could you confirm the seat number, please?
words.es: ¿Me confirma el número de butaca, por favor?
words.note: Formal.

words.en: The clerk says it leaves at 9 sharp.
words.es: El funcionario dice que sale a las 9 en punto.

words.en: Guys, let's drop the argument and go to the bus.
words.es: Chicos, dejemos la discusión y vamos al ómnibus.
words.note: Informal, to friends.

lessons.speaking: You are traveling with Sofía and Andrés, and the AI plays them and clerk Gonzalo: report what each friend said with dijo que and creía que, check the departure with Gonzalo using usted, and get everyone on the bus together.

grammar.focus: Reported speech; imperfect for background (Sofía dijo que el bus salía a las nueve, Andrés creía que era más tarde)

examples.es: Sofía dijo que el ómnibus salía a las 9.
examples.en: Sofía said the bus left at 9.

examples.es: Andrés creía que era más tarde porque miraba un mensaje viejo.
examples.en: Andrés thought it was later because he was looking at an old message.

lessons.title: Keep the Group Going Through a Highway Closure
lessons.objective: Keep a tired group motivated during a long terminal wait with clear commitments for the night and morning.

words.en: the first bus of the day
words.note: Mexico: una corrida is a scheduled bus departure.
The hours after midnight, before dawn.
Common encouragement; ¡ánimo, equipo! to a group.

words.en: Chin up, team! We're going to make it.
Tomorrow we'll leave early on the first bus.
words.es: Mañana saldremos temprano en la primera corrida.

words.en: I promise you we'll see Oaxaca, even if it's a day later.
words.es: Les prometo que veremos Oaxaca, aunque sea un día después.

words.en: We'll take turns sleeping and watching the backpacks.
words.es: Haremos turnos para dormir y cuidar las mochilas.

words.en: Hannah, you'll charge the phones and Marcus will bring dinner.
words.es: Hannah, tú cargarás los celulares y Marcus traerá la cena.
words.note: Informal: tú among friends.

words.en: I'll talk to the ticket office at 6.
words.es: Yo hablaré con la taquilla a las 6.

words.en: Excuse me, when do you expect the highway to reopen?
words.es: Disculpe, ¿cuándo esperan la reapertura de la autopista?
words.note: Formal: usted with terminal staff.

words.en: What matters is arriving safely, not arriving fast.
words.es: Lo importante es llegar bien, no llegar rápido.

lessons.speaking: You are traveling with Hannah, Marcus and Ji-woo, and the AI plays the tired group: keep them going overnight at CAPU with clear commitments in the future (mañana saldremos, yo hablaré) and encouragement like lo vamos a lograr and ¡ánimo!

grammar.focus: Future for commitments; encouragement register (mañana saldremos temprano, lo vamos a lograr, ánimo)

examples.es: Mañana saldremos temprano y llegaremos a Oaxaca al mediodía.
examples.en: Tomorrow we'll leave early and get to Oaxaca at noon.

examples.es: Yo vigilaré las mochilas y los despertaré a las 5.
examples.en: I'll watch the backpacks and wake you up at 5.

lessons.title: Your Friend, an Older Passenger, the Station Chief
lessons.objective: Switch between tú and usted with a friend, an older passenger and a station chief while asking for help.

words.note: A woman is la jefa de estación.
Polite address for an older woman, used with usted.
Chile: a change between trains, metro or buses.
Chile: feminine, la micro.
Chilean usage; elsewhere el mantenimiento.
Common in Chile for a metro or train car.
Softer than quiero; polite with staff.
Formal; with tú it is ¿te importaría…?

words.en: Tomás, calm down; we'll find another exit.
words.es: Tomás, cálmate; vamos a encontrar otra salida.
words.note: Informal: tú with a friend.

words.en: Hey, Tomás, can you wait with the lady for a minute?
words.es: Oye, Tomás, ¿me esperas con la señora un minuto?
words.note: Informal.

words.en: Do you need help with your route, Mrs. Elba?
words.es: ¿Necesita ayuda con su ruta, señora Elba?
words.note: Formal: usted with an older passenger.

words.en: Would you mind waiting for me here a moment, ma'am?
words.es: ¿Le importaría esperarme aquí un momento, señora?
words.note: Formal.

words.en: Excuse me, Mr. Muñoz, I'd like to ask you about another exit.
words.es: Disculpe, señor Muñoz, quisiera preguntarle por otra salida.
words.note: Formal.

words.en: Would it be possible to get out without stairs while they fix the lift?
words.es: ¿Sería posible salir sin escaleras mientras arreglan el ascensor?
words.note: Formal.

words.en: Would you mind walking the lady to the street?
words.es: ¿Le importaría acompañar a la señora hasta la calle?
words.note: Formal; note the personal a before la señora.

words.en: Thank you very much for your kindness, Mr. Muñoz.
words.es: Muchas gracias por su amabilidad, señor Muñoz.
words.note: Formal.

lessons.speaking: You are at a Merval station in Viña del Mar, and the AI plays your friend Tomás, señora Elba and station chief Rodrigo Muñoz: calm Tomás with tú, help señora Elba with usted, and ask about another exit with quisiera, ¿sería posible…? and ¿le importaría…?

grammar.focus: Usted / tú switching; softeners (quisiera, ¿sería posible…?, ¿le importaría…?)

examples.es: Tomás, ¿me ayudas con la maleta de la señora?
examples.en: Tomás, will you help me with the lady's suitcase?

examples.es: ¿Le importaría indicarme la salida sin escaleras, señor Muñoz?
examples.en: Would you mind showing me the step-free exit, Mr. Muñoz?

lessons.title: Escalator Fall: Report It at the Station Office
lessons.objective: Narrate a friend's escalator fall in time order to station staff and help complete the incident report.

words.note: Same form in singular and plural.
The red emergency stop button on an escalator.
La paramédica for a woman.
La testigo for a woman.
Mexican usage for the number of a report or case file.
Guadalajara's light-rail system is called el Tren Ligero.

words.en: At 8:15 we got on the escalator.
words.es: A las 8:15 subimos a la escalera eléctrica.

words.en: While we were going up, her suitcase tipped backward.
words.es: Mientras subíamos, la maleta se le fue para atrás.

words.en: Right after that, she slipped and hit her knee.
words.es: Justo después, se resbaló y se pegó en la rodilla.
words.note: Mexican usage: pegarse = to hit or bump yourself.

words.en: As soon as she fell, a young man pressed the stop button.
words.es: En cuanto se cayó, un muchacho apretó el botón de paro.

words.en: A young woman with a green backpack saw everything.
words.es: Una muchacha con mochila verde lo vio todo.

words.en: Amara, don't move; the paramedics are on their way.
words.es: Amara, no te muevas; ya vienen los paramédicos.
words.note: Informal (tú), to your friend.

words.en: Could you give me the report's reference number, please?
words.es: ¿Me da el número de folio del reporte, por favor?
words.note: Formal (usted), to station staff.

lessons.speaking: You are reporting your friend's fall, and the AI is Claudia, a station worker at Juárez station: tell what happened in order with exact times, using a las 8:15, mientras, justo después and en cuanto, and give witness details for the incident report.

grammar.focus: Past narration with time markers (a las 8:15, justo después, mientras, en cuanto llegó)

examples.es: Mientras subíamos, Amara perdió el equilibrio.
examples.en: While we were going up, Amara lost her balance.

examples.es: En cuanto llegó la paramédica, le revisó el tobillo.
examples.en: As soon as the paramedic arrived, she checked her ankle.

lessons.title: Backpack Caught in Closing Doors: Talk It Through
lessons.objective: Talk through a near miss with your group and a platform worker without blame, and agree on new habits.

words.note: The gap between the train and the platform.
Tener prisa = to be in a hurry (Spain).
Spain: the button you press to open the train doors.
Informal Spain expression for a very close call.

words.en: The door nearly caught you, Nikhil!
words.es: ¡Por poco te pilla la puerta, Nikhil!
words.note: Informal Spain: pillar = to catch or trap.

words.en: What a scare, are you okay?
words.note: Informal (tú).

words.en: We're not looking for someone to blame; we just want to understand what happened.
words.es: No buscamos culpables; solo queremos entender qué pasó.

words.en: It could have been much worse.
If the warning tone sounds, we wait for the next train.
words.es: Si suena la señal acústica, esperamos al siguiente tren.

words.en: Excuse me, what do we do if something gets caught in the door?
words.es: Perdone, ¿qué hacemos si algo se queda atrapado en la puerta?
words.note: Formal (usted), to the platform worker.

words.en: From now on, we carry our backpacks in front on the platform.
words.es: A partir de ahora, llevamos la mochila delante en el andén.

words.en: I almost ran in at the last moment too.
words.es: Yo también casi entro corriendo en el último momento.
words.note: Casi + present tense describes a past near miss.

lessons.speaking: You are going over a close call with your group, and the AI is Vicent, a platform worker at Xàtiva: talk through what happened without blaming Nikhil, using por poco, casi, podría haber sido and si clauses, and agree on new habits for the platform.

grammar.focus: Casi, por poco, podría haber; si clauses (por poco te arrastra, podría haber sido peor, si suena el pitido, esperamos)

examples.es: Por poco se cierra la puerta con la correa dentro.
examples.en: The door almost closed with the strap inside.

examples.es: Si la puerta empieza a cerrarse, no metemos la mano.
examples.en: If the door starts to close, we don't put our hand in.

lessons.title: Metrocable Stops Mid-Line: Follow the Intercom
lessons.objective: Follow intercom instructions in a stopped cable car, keep others calm, and pass on short commands.

words.note: The cable car itself on Medellín's Metrocable.
El operador for a man.
Quédense quietos = stay still (to a group).

words.en: Stay calm; the operator says it's because of the wind.
words.es: Mantengan la calma; la operadora dice que es por el viento.
words.note: Ustedes command, to the whole cabin.

words.en: If the cabin sways, we'll stay seated.
words.es: Si la cabina se balancea, nos quedaremos sentados.

words.en: Don Hernán, please sit down; that way we're all safer.
words.es: Don Hernán, siéntese, por favor; así vamos todos más seguros.
words.note: Formal (usted), to an older man.

words.en: Don't stand up, and hold on tight.
words.es: No se paren y agárrense bien.
words.note: In Colombia and Mexico, pararse = to stand up.

words.en: Copy that, Yesenia; everyone here is fine.
words.es: Recibido, Yesenia; aquí todos estamos bien.

words.en: If the wind drops, will the cabin continue to the station?
words.es: Si el viento baja, ¿la cabina seguirá hasta la estación?

words.en: How much longer do you think we'll be stopped?
words.es: ¿Cuánto tiempo más cree que estaremos detenidos?
words.note: Formal (usted), to the operator.

lessons.speaking: You are a passenger in a stopped Metrocable cabin, and the AI is operator Yesenia on the intercom and fellow passenger don Hernán: follow her instructions, pass them on with short commands like mantengan la calma, and use si + future to keep everyone seated.

grammar.focus: Si + present → future; short radio or phone commands (si se mueve, nos quedaremos sentados; mantengan la calma)

examples.es: Si el viento sigue, esperaremos aquí sentados.
examples.en: If the wind keeps up, we'll wait here seated.

examples.es: Escuchen a la operadora y no toquen la ventana.
examples.en: Listen to the operator and don't touch the window.

lessons.title: Border Control on the Mendoza–Santiago Bus
lessons.objective: Complete a customs declaration and answer border officers formally about luggage, food and documents.

words.note: The customs and agriculture form you sign at the Chilean border.
Marcar la casilla = to tick the box.
Chile and Argentina usage.
La oficial for a woman.

words.en: Good afternoon, officer; here are my passport and declaration.
words.es: Buenas tardes, oficial; aquí tiene mi pasaporte y la declaración.
words.note: Formal (usted).

words.en: I marked that I'm not carrying any animal products.
words.es: Marqué que no traigo alimentos de origen animal.

words.en: I'm here as a tourist and staying 10 days in Santiago.
words.es: Vengo por turismo y me quedo 10 días en Santiago.

words.en: Where do you declare food that wasn't marked on the form?
words.es: ¿Dónde se declaran los alimentos que no se marcaron?

words.en: Can the declaration be corrected before the inspection?
words.es: ¿Se puede corregir la declaración antes de la inspección?

words.en: Officer, my seatmate wants to declare a piece of fruit she forgot.
words.es: Oficial, mi compañera quiere declarar una fruta que olvidó.

words.en: Pilar, we'd better declare it now, before the inspection.
words.es: Pilar, mejor la declaramos ahora, antes de la inspección.
words.note: Informal (tú), to your seatmate.

words.en: Do we open the suitcase here or at the inspection table?
words.es: ¿Se abre la maleta aquí o en la mesa de inspección?

lessons.speaking: You are a bus passenger at the Los Libertadores border complex, and the AI is officer Rivas: answer formally about your luggage, food and documents, and ask how things are done with passive se, like se declaran los alimentos and se presentan los pasaportes.

grammar.focus: Formal register; passive se for procedures (se presentan los pasaportes, se declaran los alimentos)

examples.es: Aquí se declaran los alimentos antes de la inspección.
examples.en: Food is declared here before the inspection.

examples.es: Se pasan todas las maletas por la máquina de rayos X.
examples.en: All suitcases go through the X-ray machine.

lessons.title: Write the Delay Complaint at Zaragoza Delicias
lessons.objective: Write a clear formal complaint about a long delay: the facts, the times, the effects and your request.

words.note: Every business in Spain must hand you one if you ask.
Spain's usual word for a payment receipt in formal paperwork.
Formal word for money owed because of a loss or damage.
Written-register connector to open a list of facts.
Use it to introduce your request at the end.

words.en: First, the train was due to arrive at 10:15.
words.es: En primer lugar, el tren debía llegar a las 10:15.
words.note: Written register.

words.es: A continuación, el tren llegó a las 12:05.

words.en: Therefore, I missed a guided tour I had paid for in advance.
words.es: Por lo tanto, perdí una visita guiada pagada por adelantado.

words.en: Finally, I request a refund for the ticket and the tour.
words.es: Por último, solicito el reembolso del billete y de la visita.
words.note: Solicito is the formal written verb for asking.

words.en: I attach the proof of payment for the guided tour.
words.es: Adjunto el justificante de pago de la visita guiada.

words.en: Could you stamp a copy of the complaint for me?
words.es: ¿Me podría sellar una copia de la reclamación?
words.note: Formal, said to the staff member.

words.en: Excuse me, do I write only the facts here, without opinions?
words.es: Perdone, ¿escribo aquí solo los hechos, sin opiniones?
words.note: Formal.

words.en: I look forward to your reply.
words.es: Quedo a la espera de su respuesta.
words.note: Standard closing line in a formal Spanish letter.

lessons.speaking: You are the passenger, and the AI is Inés, a staff member at Zaragoza Delicias: write your formal complaint with her, giving the facts, times, effects and your request in order with en primer lugar, a continuación, por lo tanto and por último.

grammar.focus: Written register; report connectors (en primer lugar, a continuación, por lo tanto, por último)

examples.es: En primer lugar, el tren se detuvo 90 minutos cerca de Calatayud.
examples.en: First, the train stopped for 90 minutes near Calatayud.

examples.es: Por lo tanto, solicito la devolución del importe de la visita.
examples.en: Therefore, I request a refund of the amount paid for the tour.

lessons.title: Running Late: Call the Bus Line, Text the Host
lessons.objective: Call a bus company to change a booking and text a host clearly about the new arrival time.

words.note: Costa Rican word for ticket; boleto is also understood.
Common cause of road closures in Costa Rica's rainy season.
For a woman: la anfitriona.
Everyday word for a WhatsApp voice message in Central America.
Typical Costa Rican reply to gracias.

words.en: Good morning, could you put me through to reservations?
words.es: Buenos días, ¿me podría pasar con el área de reservas?
words.note: Formal, on the phone.

words.en: I'm calling to change my ticket to Monteverde because of the closure.
words.es: Llamo para cambiar mi tiquete a Monteverde por el cierre.

words.en: Could you move me to the afternoon bus, if there's room?
words.es: ¿Podría pasarme al bus de la tarde, si hay campo?
words.note: Hay campo means there's room in Costa Rica.

words.es: Con mucho gusto, espero en línea.

words.en: Could you repeat the confirmation number, please?
words.es: ¿Me podría repetir el número de confirmación, por favor?

words.en: Hello, don Rafael, I'm writing to let you know I'll arrive late.
words.es: Buenas, don Rafael, le escribo para avisarle de que llego tarde.
words.note: Polite text; use usted with an older host.

words.en: Because of the landslide, I'll arrive around 7 p.m.
words.es: Por el derrumbe, llego como a las 7 de la noche.

words.en: Could you send me the address in writing, please?
words.es: ¿Me podría mandar la dirección por escrito, por favor?
words.note: Useful when voice messages are hard to hear.

lessons.speaking: You are the traveler, and the AI is Melissa, a bus company agent, then don Rafael, your host: call to move your Monteverde ticket with ¿me podría pasar con…? and ¿podría cambiarme…?, then text don Rafael your new arrival time with le escribo para avisarle de que…

grammar.focus: Phone and text conventions; conditional politeness (¿me podría pasar con…?, le escribo para avisarle de que…)

examples.es: ¿Me podría pasar con alguien de reservas, por favor?
examples.en: Could you put me through to someone in reservations, please?

examples.es: Don Rafael, le escribo para avisarle de que el bus sale a las 2.
examples.en: Don Rafael, I'm writing to let you know the bus leaves at 2.

lessons.title: Last Day: Close Out the Pass and Plan the Airport Run
lessons.objective: Confirm the conditions for recovering a card balance and an airport route with an agent, using conditionals.

words.note: Takes the subjunctive when it means as long as: siempre que tenga.
Always followed by the subjunctive: a menos que esté lleno.

words.en: If I handed in the card today, would you refund the balance?
words.es: Si entregara la tarjeta hoy, ¿me devolverían el saldo?

words.en: So you would refund it as long as I show the receipt?
words.es: Entonces, ¿me lo devolverían siempre que presente el recibo?

words.en: And what would happen if I didn't have the purchase receipt?
words.es: ¿Y qué pasaría si no tuviera el recibo de compra?

words.en: Can it be done today, or would I have to come back another day?
words.es: ¿Se puede hacer hoy, o habría que volver otro día?

words.en: Would they let me on the Metro with 2 large suitcases?
words.es: ¿Me dejarían subir al Metro con 2 maletas grandes?

words.en: Unless there's another option, I'd take the Metro to the airport.
words.es: A menos que haya otra opción, iría en Metro al aeropuerto.

words.en: If I left at 7 in the morning, would it be very crowded?
words.es: Si saliera a las 7 de la mañana, ¿iría muy lleno?

words.en: Thank you very much, Yaritza, you helped me a lot.
words.es: Muchas gracias, Yaritza, me ayudó muchísimo.

lessons.speaking: You are the traveler, and the AI is Yaritza, an agent at Albrook station: ask what you would need to recover your card balance and whether the Metro airport route works with 2 large suitcases, using the conditional and siempre que / a menos que + subjunctive.

grammar.focus: Conditional; subjunctive in conditions (me lo devolverían siempre que tenga el recibo, a menos que…)

examples.es: Me lo devolverían siempre que la tarjeta no esté dañada.
examples.en: They would refund it to me as long as the card isn't damaged.

examples.es: Iría en Metro al aeropuerto, a menos que esté muy lleno.
examples.en: I'd take the Metro to the airport, unless it's very crowded.

lessons.title: Capstone: Strike Day from Málaga to Granada
lessons.objective: Lead a group through a strike day: teach, rebook, settle tension, handle a near miss, and report it all.

words.note: Trains legally required to run during a strike in Spain.

words.en: Guys, wait here while I ask about the minimum services.
words.es: Chicos, esperen aquí mientras pregunto por los servicios mínimos.
words.note: Ustedes command, used with a group of friends.

words.en: Excuse me, could you tell me which trains to Granada are guaranteed?
words.es: Disculpe, ¿podría decirme qué trenes a Granada están garantizados?
words.note: Formal.

words.en: I suggest we take the bus if they cancel the train.
words.es: Les propongo que cojamos el autobús si cancelan el tren.
words.note: In Spain coger means to take a bus or train.

words.en: I understand you're tired, but we'll get to Granada today.
words.es: Entiendo que estén cansados, pero llegaremos a Granada hoy.

words.en: Kofi, step back! Don't get close to the edge.
words.es: ¡Kofi, atrás! No te acerques al borde.
words.note: Informal tú.

words.en: I wanted to report that my friend nearly fell onto the tracks.
words.es: Quería avisar de que mi amigo casi se cae a la vía.
words.note: Formal, said to station staff.

words.en: Consequently, I request a refund of the train ticket.
words.es: Por consiguiente, solicito la devolución del billete de tren.
words.note: Written register.

words.en: Lucía, I'm writing to let you know: we'll arrive around 22:00.
words.es: Lucía, te escribo para avisarte: llegamos sobre las 22:00.
words.note: Informal text; sobre means around with times in Spain.

lessons.speaking: You lead friends Marta and Kofi, and the AI plays station staff, your friends and your host: check minimum services, rebook onto the bus, settle tension, then write the complaint and text the host, using commands, les recomiendo que + subjunctive, the conditional and connectors.

grammar.focus: Capstone: integrating the Master 20 grammar

examples.es: Les recomiendo que esperen detrás de la línea hasta que pare el tren.
examples.en: I recommend you wait behind the line until the train stops.

examples.es: Si hubiera plazas en el autobús, llegaríamos a Granada antes de las 20:00.
examples.en: If there were seats on the bus, we'd reach Granada before 20:00.
